claims.statement: The National Park Service dates residential and ceremonial use of Poverty Point to approximately 1700–1100 BCE.
Hunter-fisher-gatherers built monumental earthworks in the Lower Mississippi Valley and participated in far-reaching exchange networks.
The map uses UNESCO’s reference position for Poverty Point’s mound builders, not a territorial boundary.

evidence.note: This follows the NPS World Heritage article’s date range, not a date for each mound. UNESCO’s BP wording has not been converted into calendar years. The marker locates the site, not its trading network.
